afghanistan.name: Afghanistan
afghanistan.dish_note: Fragrant rice with lamb, carrots, raisins and warm spices — commonly served for gatherings and celebrations.
afghanistan.personality_story: A Pashtun leader who consolidated power after the death of Nader Shah and founded the Durrani Empire. He unified key tribes and territories, establishing political foundations often linked to the emergence of a modern Afghan state identity.

albania.name: Albania
albania.dish_note: Baked lamb with rice in tangy yogurt sauce — a hearty Ottoman-influenced comfort food central to family meals.
albania.personality_story: National hero who led resistance against Ottoman expansion for 25 years. His legacy as defender of Albanian independence is central to national identity, and his image appears everywhere from statues to currency.

algeria.name: Algeria
algeria.dish_note: Steamed semolina with vegetables and meat in rich broth — a Berber staple central to family meals, traditionally served Fridays.
algeria.personality_story: Religious and military leader who led resistance against French colonization in the 1830s-40s. Known for chivalrous treatment of prisoners, he's revered as a national hero and symbol of dignity in resistance.

andorra.name: Andorra
andorra.dish_note: Mashed cabbage and potatoes with pork fat or bacon — hearty Catalan mountain comfort food perfect for cold winters.
andorra.personality_story: According to legend, Charlemagne granted Andorra its independence in 778 as thanks for help fighting Moors. While historically uncertain, this origin story is central to national identity and the unique co-principality structure.

angola.name: Angola
angola.dish_note: Chicken stewed in palm oil with garlic, okra, and peppers, served with funge — a rich dish blending African and Portuguese influences.
angola.personality_story: Poet, physician, and revolutionary who became Angola's first president after independence in 1975. His writings inspired the liberation movement, and he's revered as the father of the nation despite leading during civil war.

argentina.name: Argentina
argentina.dish_note: Argentine barbecue featuring premium beef grilled over wood or charcoal — a social ritual central to culture, especially Sunday family gatherings.
argentina.personality_story: First Lady and political icon who championed workers' and women's rights. Her populist legacy divides Argentina still — revered by some as a saint, criticized by others as a demagogue. Her story inspired the famous musical.

armenia.name: Armenia
armenia.dish_note: Armenian barbecue with marinated meat grilled over charcoal, served with lavash and fresh herbs — central to social gatherings.
armenia.personality_story: Linguist and theologian who created the Armenian alphabet in 405 AD, enabling translation of the Bible and preservation of Armenian culture through centuries of foreign domination. His invention is celebrated annually and remains central to Armenian identity.

australia.name: Australia
australia.dish_note: Pavlova: meringue dessert with fruit and cream. Or meat pie — portable pastry with meat filling, an Aussie staple. Food culture is multicultural fusion.
australia.personality_story: Wildlife expert and TV personality who became global ambassador for Australian wildlife and conservation. His enthusiastic 'Crikey!' approach introduced millions to Australia's unique fauna. Tragically killed by stingray in 2006, but remains cultural icon.

austria.name: Austria
austria.dish_note: Breaded and fried veal cutlet served with potato salad — ubiquitous classic. Must be veal to be authentic; pork is 'Schnitzel Wiener Art.'
austria.personality_story: Child prodigy composer who revolutionized classical music. Though born in Salzburg, his legacy permeates Austrian culture. Ironically, Mozart died poor and was buried in an unmarked grave, yet now generates massive tourism revenue and cultural prestige.

azerbaijan.name: Azerbaijan
azerbaijan.dish_note: Saffron rice with meat, dried fruits, and chestnuts, cooked in layers with crispy bottom — central to celebrations and culinary identity.
azerbaijan.personality_story: Persian poet born in Ganja (Azerbaijan) whose romantic epic poetry influenced Islamic literature. His works (like 'Layla and Majnun') are considered masterpieces. He's celebrated as part of Azerbaijani cultural heritage despite writing in Persian.

bahamas.name: Bahamas
bahamas.dish_note: Fresh conch with tomatoes, onions, peppers, and citrus — central to Bahamian food culture. Also enjoyed fried as fritters or in chowder.
bahamas.personality_story: First Prime Minister of independent Bahamas (1973-1992), leader of the Majority Rule movement that ended white minority rule. Called 'Father of the Nation,' though his legacy is mixed due to later corruption allegations. His leadership shaped modern Bahamas.

bahrain.name: Bahrain
bahrain.dish_note: Spiced rice with meat cooked with dried limes, cardamom, saffron — Gulf comfort food representing traditional Bahraini hospitality.
bahrain.personality_story: Founder of modern Bahrain, expelled Persian occupiers in 1783 and established Al Khalifa dynasty that still rules today. The current King and Grand Mosque are named after him, cementing his place as national founder.

bangladesh.name: Bangladesh
bangladesh.dish_note: Prized hilsa fish in mustard sauce — culturally iconic and celebrated in Bengali poetry and cuisine. Hilsa season is a major event.
bangladesh.personality_story: Founding father of Bangladesh, led independence movement from Pakistan in 1971. Became first president but was assassinated in 1975 coup. His daughter Sheikh Hasina later became Prime Minister. He's revered as 'Bangabandhu' (Friend of Bengal).

belarus.name: Belarus
belarus.dish_note: Crispy grated potato pancakes served with sour cream — simple comfort food reflecting agricultural heritage and Soviet-era cuisine.
belarus.personality_story: President since 1994, often called 'Europe's last dictator.' Former collective farm director who maintained Soviet system. His authoritarian rule has lasted nearly 30 years through manipulated elections, repression, and close Russia ties.

belgium.name: Belgium
belgium.dish_note: Steamed mussels with white wine and garlic served with crispy fries and mayo — Belgian comfort food. Fries were invented here, not France.
belgium.personality_story: Creator of Tintin comic series, one of most influential European comics. Tintin adventures shaped childhoods across Europe and beyond. Hergé's ligne claire (clear line) art style influenced generations. Brussels has Tintin murals throughout city.

belize.name: Belize
belize.dish: Rice and Beans with Stewed Chicken
belize.dish_note: Red beans in coconut milk with rice, stewed chicken, potato salad, and plantains — Creole comfort food found everywhere.
belize.personality_story: Father of Belize's independence, led the nation from British colony to independence in 1981. Served as Prime Minister and is revered for peaceful transition. His vision shaped modern Belizean identity balancing Caribbean and Central American influences.

benin.name: Benin
benin.dish_note: Corn dough porridge with tomato sauce and meat/fish — filling traditional comfort food representing staple-based Beninese cuisine.
benin.personality_story: Last independent king of Dahomey who resisted French colonization in the 1890s. Eventually defeated and exiled, he's remembered as symbol of resistance and African sovereignty. His legacy inspires national pride.

bhutan.name: Bhutan
bhutan.dish_note: Fiery chili peppers in cheese sauce served with red rice — intensely spicy and served at nearly every meal. Reflects Bhutanese love of chilies.
bhutan.personality_story: The beloved king who introduced Gross National Happiness concept and voluntarily transitioned Bhutan from absolute monarchy to constitutional monarchy (2008). His wisdom and selflessness shaped modern Bhutan's unique development philosophy.

bolivia.name: Bolivia
bolivia.dish_note: Savory pastries with spiced meat, potatoes, and juicy filling — eaten mid-morning as snack. Bolivia's sweeter answer to empanadas.
bolivia.personality_story: First indigenous president (2006-2019), former coca grower who nationalized gas industry and championed indigenous rights. Controversial figure — praised for poverty reduction, criticized for authoritarianism. Resigned amid election fraud allegations and fled to Mexico. His legacy divides Bolivia.

bosnia-and-herzegovina.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
bosnia-and-herzegovina.dish_note: Small grilled sausages in flatbread with onions, kajmak, and ajvar — ubiquitous Balkan street food representing Ottoman culinary legacy.
bosnia-and-herzegovina.personality_story: Young Bosnian Serb who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo (1914), triggering WWI. Viewed as hero by some, terrorist by others. His legacy is deeply controversial and reflects Bosnia's complex national identities and histories.

botswana.name: Botswana
botswana.dish_note: Slow-cooked, shredded beef or goat pounded in mortar, served with pap — traditional communal dish central to celebrations.
botswana.personality_story: Founding president who led Botswana from British protectorate to independence (1966). His interracial marriage to British woman caused scandal in apartheid-era Southern Africa. He governed wisely, laying foundations for Botswana's stability and prosperity. National hero and model leader.

brazil.name: Brazil
brazil.dish_note: Black bean stew with pork served with rice, farofa, collards, and oranges — heavy Saturday lunch tradition central to culinary identity.
brazil.personality_story: Football legend who won 3 World Cups and became global icon. Beyond sport, he represented Brazilian excellence and joy. His death (2022) brought national mourning. Football in Brazil isn't just sport — it's identity, hope, and art.

brunei.name: Brunei
brunei.dish_note: Sticky sago starch eaten with bamboo fork dipped in sour/spicy sauces — traditional but challenging taste, like eating glue paste.
brunei.personality_story: World's longest-reigning current monarch and one of richest men globally. Absolute ruler who uses oil wealth to provide welfare state for citizens while maintaining strict Islamic conservatism. Personality cult is omnipresent — his image is everywhere.

bulgaria.name: Bulgaria
bulgaria.dish_note: Shopska: tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers with crumbled sirene cheese. Banitsa: cheese phyllo pastry. Both are staples of Bulgarian cuisine.
bulgaria.personality_story: Revolutionary hero who fought Ottoman rule and envisioned democratic, ethnically inclusive Bulgaria. Executed by Ottomans in 1873, he became martyr and national symbol. His idealism contrasts with modern cynicism but remains culturally important.

burkina-faso.name: Burkina Faso
burkina-faso.dish_note: Shopska: tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers with crumbled sirene cheese. Banitsa: cheese phyllo pastry. Both are staples of Bulgarian cuisine.
burkina-faso.personality_story: Revolutionary hero who fought Ottoman rule and envisioned democratic, ethnically inclusive Bulgaria. Executed by Ottomans in 1873, he became martyr and national symbol. His idealism contrasts with modern cynicism but remains culturally important.

cambodia.name: Cambodia
cambodia.dish_note: Fish curry steamed in banana leaves with coconut milk, lemongrass, and spices — fragrant, delicate, distinctly Khmer, balancing Thai/Vietnamese influences.
cambodia.personality_story: Former king, politician, filmmaker — dominated Cambodian politics for 60 years. He navigated independence, civil war, Khmer Rouge, Vietnamese occupation, and restoration. Controversial figure — praised for independence, criticized for enabling Khmer Rouge. Died 2012.

cameroon.name: Cameroon
cameroon.dish_note: Bitterleaf stew with peanuts and meat/fish — labor-intensive preparation, richly flavored, central to celebrations and Cameroonian identity.
cameroon.personality_story: President since 1982, one of Africa's longest-ruling leaders. His increasingly authoritarian rule, corruption, and mismanagement have impoverished the country despite resources. The Anglophone crisis erupted under his watch. He's rarely in country, often in Switzerland.

canada.name: Canada
canada.dish_note: Fries with cheese curds and gravy — Quebec-born, now pan-Canadian comfort food. Simple, indulgent, perfect post-hockey. Represents unpretentious Canadian identity.
canada.personality_story: Cancer survivor who ran across Canada with prosthetic leg to raise cancer awareness (1980). He ran 5,373km before cancer returned; he died at 22. His Marathon of Hope became Canadian legend. Annual Terry Fox Runs worldwide raised $850M+. He embodies Canadian values: determination, selflessness, humility.

central-african-republic.name: Central African Republic
central-african-republic.dish_note: Cassava paste with peanut and palm oil sauces. Bush meat, dried fish, smoked catfish from the Ubangi River. Congo Basin cuisine with minimal French influence outside Bangui restaurants.
central-african-republic.personality_story: CAR's most notorious figure. Army commander who seized power in 1966, Bokassa ruled for 13 years, crowning himself Emperor in 1977 in a ceremony that cost $30M (80% of the national budget) and was attended by no foreign heads of state. In 1979, he ordered the massacre of over 100 schoolchildren who protested against wearing expensive school uniforms his company manufactured. France — his former colonial patron and personal benefactor — finally intervened militarily to remove him. He died in 1996. His coronation robes are in a Paris museum.
sectors: Diamond mining (significant producer — Kimberley Process sanctioned 2013–16)

chad.name: Chad
chad.dish: Boule de mil / Sauce gombo / Daraba
chad.dish_note: Millet balls with okra or peanut stew — the daily staple. N'Djamena has Lebanese and Chinese restaurants for variety.
chad.personality_story: Military officer who seized power in December 1990 and ruled Chad for 30 years. An ethnic Zaghawa from the north, he survived 8 major rebel offensives using his tribal network and French military backing. Secured the Chad-Cameroon oil pipeline and positioned Chad as the West's counter-terrorism anchor in the Sahel. Died April 20, 2021 — the day after winning a 6th presidential term — killed commanding troops against the FACT rebel group at the northern front. His son Mahamat took power immediately, bypassing the constitution. Legacy: 30 years of forced stability, oil revenues without development, and a military dynasty in the making.

chile.name: Chile
chile.dish_note: Corn pie with beef, chicken, egg, olives, and sweet corn topping — blends indigenous and Spanish influences, served hot in clay dishes.
chile.personality_story: Socialist president (1970-73) who nationalized copper and implemented radical reforms. Overthrown in CIA-backed coup led by Pinochet. Died defending presidential palace. His legacy divides Chile — socialist hero vs failed experiment. The coup led to brutal Pinochet dictatorship (1973-90) that still haunts Chile.

china.name: China
china.dish_note: Peking Duck: roasted with crispy skin, served with pancakes. Or dumplings (jiaozi) — universally Chinese. Regional cuisines vary dramatically.
china.personality_story: Leader who initiated 'Reform and Opening Up' (1978) transforming China from isolated communist economy to market-oriented powerhouse. His pragmatism ('It doesn't matter if a cat is black or white, as long as it catches mice') enabled China's rise. Tiananmen Square crackdown (1989) is dark legacy.

colombia.name: Colombia
colombia.dish_note: Massive platter with beans, rice, meats, egg, plantain, avocado, arepa — from Antioquia, represents paisa hospitality and heartiness.
colombia.personality_story: Nobel Prize-winning author of 'One Hundred Years of Solitude' who defined magical realism and put Colombian literature on world stage. 'Gabo' is national treasure. His work captured Colombian history, violence, and magical beauty. He died 2014.

costa-rica.name: Costa Rica
costa-rica.dish_note: Rice and beans with Lizano sauce — breakfast staple, simple and ubiquitous, central to Tico identity. Every household has their recipe.
costa-rica.personality_story: President who abolished the military in 1948 after civil war, redirecting budget to healthcare and education. This decision shaped Costa Rica's peaceful identity. He also nationalized banks and gave women and Afro-Caribbeans voting rights. National hero.

cote-d-ivoire.name: Cote d'Ivoire
cote-d-ivoire.dish_note: Fermented cassava couscous with grilled fish, tomato sauce, and chili — ubiquitous street food, represents Ivorian identity across classes.
cote-d-ivoire.personality_story: First president (1960-1993) and 'father of the nation.' His 33-year rule brought stability and pro-French policies but also personality cult. He built Yamoussoukro Basilica (larger than St. Peter's) in his home village at enormous cost. Controversial legacy — stability vs authoritarianism.

croatia.name: Croatia
croatia.dish_note: Meat/octopus and vegetables slow-cooked under iron bell with hot coals — regional variations, represents Dalmatian cooking tradition.
croatia.personality_story: First president of independent Croatia (1990-1999), led country through independence war but ruled with authoritarian tendencies. Controversial figure — hero of independence to some, nationalist criticized for corruption to others. Died 1999.

cuba.name: Cuba
cuba.dish_note: Shredded beef in tomato sauce with rice and beans — 'old clothes' dish. However, beef shortages make it rare despite being national symbol.
cuba.personality_story: Revolutionary leader who overthrew Batista (1959) and ruled until 2008. His alliance with USSR shaped Cold War. Polarizing figure — hero of anti-imperialism to supporters, brutal dictator to critics. His legacy dominates Cuba. Died 2016.

cyprus.name: Cyprus
cyprus.dish_note: Halloumi: grillable cheese, Cypriot pride. Or Meze: extensive small plates representing hospitality. Both are central to food culture.
cyprus.personality_story: First president of independent Cyprus (1960-1977), Orthodox archbishop who fought for independence from Britain and against Turkish intervention. Father of the nation. His legacy is complicated by ethnic tensions but he's revered by Greek Cypriots.

czech-republic.name: Czech Republic
czech-republic.dish_note: Beef sirloin in creamy vegetable sauce with bread dumplings, cranberries, whipped cream — hearty Czech comfort food. Beer essential.
czech-republic.personality_story: Playwright, dissident, and first president of post-communist Czechoslovakia (1989-92) then Czech Republic (1993-2003). Velvet Revolution leader who brought democracy peacefully. Intellectual president who brought moral authority. National hero. Died 2011.

democratic-republic-of-the-congo.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.dish_note: Chicken in palm nut sauce with rice — rich, oily Congolese staple. However, food insecurity means many can't afford regularly.
democratic-republic-of-the-congo.personality_story: First democratically elected Prime Minister who led independence from Belgium (1960). Assassinated in 1961 with Belgian and US involvement. Pan-African hero and martyr. His murder symbolizes Cold War interference and neo-colonialism. National icon.

denmark.name: Denmark
denmark.dish_note: Smørrebrød: elaborate open-faced rye sandwiches. Frikadeller: meatballs. Danish cuisine is hearty, pork-heavy, New Nordic movement evolved it.
denmark.personality_story: Fairy tale author ('Little Mermaid,' 'Ugly Duckling') who became global literary figure. His stories blend melancholy and magic. The Little Mermaid statue is Copenhagen icon. Andersen represents Danish cultural export and melancholic Nordic soul.

dominican-republic.name: Dominican Republic
dominican-republic.dish_note: Rice, beans, meat, salad — 'The Flag' represents everyday Dominican lunch. Simple, filling, ubiquitous. Street food culture is vibrant.
dominican-republic.personality_story: Founding father who led independence from Haiti (1844). National hero and symbol of Dominican sovereignty. Exiled most of life, died in poverty, but legacy shapes national identity. Revered across political spectrum.

ecuador.name: Ecuador
ecuador.dish_note: Raw fish/shrimp in citrus marinade — coastal classic. Interior prefers locro, hornado, or cuy. Regional cuisines vary significantly.
ecuador.personality_story: President (2007-2017) who implemented 'Citizens' Revolution' — leftist policies, increased social spending, infrastructure investment. Reduced poverty but also increased debt and centralized power. Polarizing figure — hero to supporters, authoritarian to critics. Lives in Belgium avoiding corruption charges.

egypt.name: Egypt
egypt.dish_note: Rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas with fried onions and tomato sauce — cheap street food comfort. Or Ful Medames (fava beans) for breakfast.
egypt.personality_story: Revolutionary leader and president (1956-70) who nationalized Suez Canal, championed Pan-Arabism, and modernized Egypt. Hero to millions across Arab world. His legacy shapes Egyptian national identity. Aswan Dam and socialist policies defined era.

el-salvador.name: El Salvador
el-salvador.dish_note: Thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans, or pork, served with curtido and salsa — ubiquitous, cheap, national pride.
el-salvador.personality_story: Archbishop assassinated in 1980 while saying mass for speaking against government violence during civil war. Martyr and symbol of justice. Canonized by Catholic Church in 2018. His legacy inspires human rights advocacy.

estonia.name: Estonia
estonia.dish_note: Dark rye bread with pickled herring, sour cream, onions — hearty, functional, central to identity. Or blood sausage (verivorst).
estonia.personality_story: Minimalist composer creating hauntingly beautiful sacred music. His 'tintinnabuli' style is internationally acclaimed. Living national treasure. His music captures Estonian soul — contemplative, spiritual, sparse. He represents cultural excellence of small nation.

ethiopia.name: Ethiopia
ethiopia.dish_note: Spongy teff flatbread with spicy stews — unique, flavorful, eaten with hands. Coffee ceremony is elaborate cultural ritual.
ethiopia.personality_story: Emperor (1930-74) who modernized Ethiopia and represented it globally. Deity figure in Rastafari religion. Overthrown in communist coup (1974). His reign shaped modern Ethiopia and Pan-African movement. Complex legacy — modernizer vs autocrat.

finland.name: Finland
finland.dish_note: Rye pastries with rice/potato or salmon soup — simple, hearty Finnish food utilizing local ingredients. Coffee consumption is world's highest.
finland.personality_story: Composer whose symphonies and tone poems (Finlandia) became synonymous with Finnish national identity during independence struggle from Russia. His music captures Finnish landscape and spirit. National treasure and cultural icon.

france.name: France
france.dish_note: Braised chicken in wine or beef stew — regional cuisines vary immensely. Baguette, cheese, wine are sacred. UNESCO heritage cuisine.
france.personality_story: General who led Free French Forces in WWII and later became president, founding Fifth Republic (1958). His vision of French grandeur and independence shaped modern France. Airport, aircraft carrier, and countless streets named after him.

gabon.name: Gabon
gabon.dish_note: Chicken in palm nut sauce or smoked fish — Central African cuisine. Cassava, plantains, palm oil staples. French colonial influence.
gabon.personality_story: President (1967-2009, 42 years) who dominated Gabon's oil era. Converted to Islam (1973). Accumulated massive wealth (corruption), maintained French ties, funded infrastructure (Transgabonais railway). Died 2009; son Ali Bongo succeeded. Bongo dynasty ruled 56 years total (1967-2023).

georgia.name: Georgia
georgia.dish_note: Cheese-filled bread (various styles) or soup dumplings — Georgian cuisine is hearty, wine-paired, centered on supra feast tradition.
georgia.personality_story: Medieval poet who wrote 'The Knight in the Panther's Skin,' Georgia's national epic. His romantic chivalric poem shaped Georgian literary identity. Tbilisi's main avenue is named after him. Literary icon transcending centuries.

germany.name: Germany
germany.dish_note: Sausages, breaded cutlet, curry sausage — hearty meat-heavy cuisine. Regional variations significant. Bread culture is serious (300+ types).
germany.personality_story: First Chancellor of West Germany (1949-63) who rebuilt post-WWII Germany, anchored it in West, and laid foundations for European integration. His leadership shaped modern democratic Germany. Age 73 when elected — proved competence over youth.

ghana.name: Ghana
ghana.dish_note: Tomato rice (Ghana vs Nigeria rivalry is real) or pounded cassava/plantain with soup — starchy, spicy, palm oil-based cuisine.
ghana.personality_story: Independence leader (1957) and first president, Pan-African visionary who inspired continent-wide liberation movements. 'Seek ye first the political kingdom' was his motto. Overthrown in 1966 coup but legacy as African independence icon endures. Mausoleum in Accra.

greece.name: Greece
greece.dish_note: Layered eggplant-meat-béchamel bake or fresh salad with feta — Mediterranean healthy cuisine, olive oil-based, mezze culture.
greece.personality_story: Athenian statesman who led during Golden Age, built Parthenon, and promoted democracy. His funeral oration defined democratic values. Ancient but legacy shapes Greek identity and Western civilization. 'What you leave behind is not what is engraved in stone monuments, but what is woven into the lives of others.'

guatemala.name: Guatemala
guatemala.dish_note: Complex meat stew with seeds and roasted vegetables — pre-Columbian Maya dish representing indigenous heritage. Or Kak'ik (turkey soup).
guatemala.personality_story: Indigenous K'iche' Maya activist who won 1992 Nobel Peace Prize for work on indigenous rights and social justice. Her autobiography exposed civil war atrocities against Maya. Controversial figure but symbol of indigenous resistance.

guyana.name: Guyana
guyana.dish_note: Cassareep stew, Indian flatbread, or one-pot rice — Caribbean-South American fusion. Indian/African/Amerindian/Chinese influenced.
guyana.personality_story: First Premier/President (1950s, 1992-97), Indo-Guyanese leader, Marxist who founded PPP (People's Progressive Party). His wife Janet Jagan succeeded him. Represents Indo-Guyanese political power and socialist era. Died 1997. Airport named after him.

haiti.name: Haiti
haiti.dish_note: Fried pork or pumpkin soup — Creole cuisine (African/French/Taíno). But 5M+ face acute hunger. Food is scarce.
haiti.personality_story: Leader of Haitian Revolution (slave revolt 1791-1804) against France. Military genius who defeated French, Spanish, British. Captured by Napoleon (1802), died in French prison (1803). Haiti achieved independence 1804 under Dessalines. Louverture is hero of Black liberation globally.

honduras.name: Honduras
honduras.dish_note: Tortilla with beans or conch soup — Central American staple. Beans, rice, tortillas. Indigenous/Spanish/Garífuna influenced.
honduras.personality_story: Indigenous Lenca environmental activist who fought Agua Zarca Dam (threatened indigenous land, rivers). Assassinated 2016 (gunmen killed her at home). International outcry. Her murder exposed violence against activists. Won Goldman Prize posthumously. Represents Honduras' environmental/indigenous rights struggle.

hungary.name: Hungary
hungary.dish_note: Paprika-spiced beef soup — hearty, warming, quintessentially Hungarian. Or Chicken Paprikash. Cuisine is heavy, meat-based, paprika-dominated.
hungary.personality_story: Prime Minister who led 1956 anti-Soviet uprising, declaring Hungary's withdrawal from Warsaw Pact. Uprising was crushed by Soviet tanks; Nagy was executed. He's national hero and martyr. His reburial (1989) marked communism's end.

iceland.name: Iceland
iceland.dish_note: Fermented shark (intense) or lamb soup or thick yogurt — historically survival food, now modern cuisine is excellent. Hot dogs are beloved.
iceland.personality_story: First elected female head of state globally (President 1980-96). Single mother who championed language preservation and culture. Her election was groundbreaking. She represents Iceland's gender equality leadership.

india.name: India
india.dish_note: No single dish — incredible regional diversity. North: butter chicken, biryani. South: dosa, idli. Coastal: seafood curries. Vegetarianism common.
india.personality_story: Independence leader who pioneered nonviolent resistance (satyagraha) against British rule. Assassinated 1948. His philosophy inspired civil rights movements globally. 'Father of the Nation' — complex legacy but towering historical figure.

indonesia.name: Indonesia
indonesia.dish_note: Fried rice with sweet soy or slow-cooked beef curry — regional cuisines vary dramatically. Street food culture is vibrant and delicious.
indonesia.personality_story: First president and independence leader who proclaimed independence from Netherlands (1945). Charismatic orator who championed non-aligned movement. Overthrown in 1965-66 coup/purge that killed 500,000+. His daughter Megawati later became president. Founding father.

iran.name: Iran
iran.dish_note: Saffron rice with grilled meat kebabs, tomato, sumac — ubiquitous Persian dish. Or herb stew (Ghormeh Sabzi). Sophisticated, aromatic cuisine.
iran.personality_story: Founded Persian Empire, issued Cyrus Cylinder (first human rights charter), freed Jews from Babylon. Ancient but represents Persian civilization's golden age and source of national pride. Pre-Islamic glory invoked by many Iranians.

iraq.name: Iraq
iraq.dish_note: Grilled Tigris carp with tamarind and spices — Baghdad specialty. Or Quzi (roasted lamb). Iraqi cuisine blends Arab, Persian, Turkish influences.
iraq.personality_story: Babylonian king who created Hammurabi's Code — one of earliest written legal codes. 'Eye for an eye' comes from this. Ancient Mesopotamian glory represents Iraq's historical importance as cradle of civilization before modern tragedy.

ireland.name: Ireland
ireland.dish_note: Lamb with potatoes, onions, carrots — hearty comfort food. Or Boxty, full Irish breakfast. Modern Irish cuisine is excellent now.
ireland.personality_story: Modernist writer whose 'Ulysses' and 'Dubliners' captured Irish life and revolutionized literature. He left Ireland but wrote obsessively about Dublin. Bloomsday (June 16) celebrates Ulysses. Literary tradition is Ireland's cultural wealth.

israel.name: Israel
israel.dish_note: Chickpea falafel in pita or hummus — staples of Israeli/Middle Eastern cuisine. Or shakshuka. Food culture blends Jewish diaspora traditions.
israel.personality_story: Founding father and first Prime Minister who declared Israel's independence (1948). Labor Zionist who shaped state's early ideology and institutions. His vision of Jewish homeland shapes modern Israel. Airport named after him.

italy.name: Italy
italy.dish_note: No single dish — regional cuisines differ dramatically. Pizza (Naples), Carbonara (Rome), Risotto (Milan), Ragù (Bologna). Food is religion.
italy.personality_story: Renaissance polymath — artist, inventor, scientist. Mona Lisa, Last Supper, flying machine designs. He represents Italian Renaissance genius that shaped Western civilization. Symbol of human potential and Italian cultural contribution.

jamaica.name: Jamaica
jamaica.dish_note: Ackee fruit with salted cod for breakfast, or spicy jerk chicken — flavorful, African/British/Indian influenced cuisine.
jamaica.personality_story: Reggae legend who brought Jamaican music and Rastafari culture to global stage. Songs like 'One Love,' 'Redemption Song' became anthems. Died 1981 at 36. His legacy is Jamaica's greatest cultural export. Museum in Kingston is pilgrimage site.

japan.name: Japan
japan.dish_note: No single dish — sushi, ramen, or curry rice represent cuisine. Regional specialties vary. Food culture is refined, seasonal, presentation-focused.
japan.personality_story: Emperor during Meiji Restoration (1868-1912) that modernized Japan from feudal state to world power. Industrialization, constitution, military buildup transformed nation. His reign shaped modern Japan. Era named after him.

jordan.name: Jordan
jordan.dish_note: Lamb in fermented yogurt over rice — Bedouin traditional dish served at celebrations, eaten with hands. Represents hospitality.
jordan.personality_story: Ruled 1952-99, navigated Cold War, Arab-Israeli wars, and regional turmoil. Made peace with Israel (1994). Father of current King Abdullah II. His moderate leadership shaped modern Jordan. Died 1999; massive outpouring of grief.

kazakhstan.name: Kazakhstan
kazakhstan.dish_note: Boiled horse meat with flat noodles — 'five fingers' eaten by hand, represents nomadic heritage. Or horse sausage (kazy). Meat-heavy cuisine.
kazakhstan.personality_story: First president (1991-2019) who led Kazakhstan from Soviet republic to independent nation. Authoritarian ruler who built Astana from scratch and accumulated vast wealth. Stepped down 2019 but retained influence. Capital was renamed Nur-Sultan after him (changed back to Astana 2022).

kenya.name: Kenya
kenya.dish_note: Grilled goat/beef with ugali (maize porridge) and kachumbari salad — social food eaten at gatherings. Or sukuma wiki (collard greens).
kenya.personality_story: First president and independence leader (1963-78). 'Mzee' (elder) who led Kenya from British colony to nation. His legacy is complex — founding father but also authoritarian. His son Uhuru was president 2013-22. Airport named after him.

kosovo.name: Kosovo
kosovo.dish_note: Layered pancake, lamb-yogurt, or grilled meat — Balkan-Ottoman cuisine. Albanian/Serbian/Turkish influenced. Coffee culture strong.
kosovo.personality_story: First President (1992-2006), 'Gandhi of the Balkans' for non-violent resistance to Serbian rule (1990s). Led LDK party, parallel government during occupation. Died 2006 (lung cancer). Represents Kosovo's peaceful resistance before war. Scarf was signature.

kuwait.name: Kuwait
kuwait.dish_note: Spiced rice with meat — Gulf Arabic staple similar to biryani. Or gabout (dumplings). Cuisine has Indian/Persian influences.
kuwait.personality_story: Emir during Iraqi invasion (1990). Fled to Saudi Arabia; coalition forces liberated Kuwait (1991). Returned and rebuilt country. His leadership during crisis shaped modern Kuwait. Died 2006. Al-Sabah family has ruled since 1750s.

kyrgyzstan.name: Kyrgyzstan
kyrgyzstan.dish_note: Boiled horse meat with flat noodles — 'five fingers' eaten by hand, represents nomadic heritage. Or plov (rice pilaf).
kyrgyzstan.personality_story: President (2005-10) who came to power in Tulip Revolution (2005) but became corrupt and authoritarian. Overthrown in 2010 revolution (100+ killed). His fall shows pattern of Kyrgyz politics — revolution, corruption, revolution again. He fled to Belarus.

laos.name: Laos
laos.dish_note: Minced meat salad with herbs and roasted rice powder, or green papaya salad — eaten with sticky rice. Similar to Thai but less sweet.
laos.personality_story: Communist revolutionary leader and first president of Lao PDR (1975-92). Led Pathet Lao to victory over royalists. His policies shaped modern Laos. National hero to government; controversial figure to royalists. Died 1992.

latvia.name: Latvia
latvia.dish: Grey Peas and Bacon / Rye Bread
latvia.dish_note: Boiled gray peas with bacon, or dense dark rye bread — peasant food reflecting agricultural heritage. Simple, hearty, carb-heavy cuisine.
latvia.personality_story: First female president of Latvia (1999-2007) and Eastern Europe. Born in Latvia, fled Soviet occupation as child, returned after independence. Her presidency stabilized Latvia and led to EU/NATO membership. She represents Latvia's post-Soviet transformation.

lebanon.name: Lebanon
lebanon.dish_note: Array of small dishes (hummus, tabbouleh, baba ghanoush) or bulgur-meat kibbeh — Levantine cuisine excellence despite economic crisis.
lebanon.personality_story: Poet, writer, artist whose 'The Prophet' is one of best-selling books ever. Lebanese-American who captured Lebanese soul — mysticism, beauty, exile. Represents Lebanon's cultural contribution to world despite small size.

liberia.name: Liberia
liberia.dish_note: Cassava dumpling, greens with palm oil, or rice — West African staple. Indigenous and American freedmen influenced.
liberia.personality_story: Africa's first elected female president (2006-18). Nobel Peace Prize (2011) for women's rights, peace work. Led post-war rebuilding, managed Ebola crisis. 'Iron Lady of Africa.' Faced criticism for son's corruption but represents hope, recovery. Liberia's transformation leader.

libya.name: Libya
libya.dish_note: Couscous with meat or barley dough with stew — North African Maghrebi cuisine but food security is issue due to conflict.
libya.personality_story: Eccentric dictator (1969-2011) who ruled 42 years. Green Book ideology, bizarre speeches at UN, sponsoring terrorism, then reconciliation with West. Overthrown in 2011 uprising, killed brutally. His death triggered chaos continuing today.

liechtenstein.name: Liechtenstein
liechtenstein.dish_note: Cheese noodles or cornmeal — Alpine comfort food. Similar to Swiss/Austrian cuisine. Cheese, potatoes, sausages. Expensive restaurants.
liechtenstein.personality_story: Reigning Prince since 1989. Transformed Liechtenstein from tax haven to legitimate finance center. Increased Prince's powers (2003 referendum — can dissolve parliament, veto laws). Wealthy (owns LGT Bank). Day-to-day rule delegated to son Alois (2004). Represents modern constitutional monarchy with real power.

lithuania.name: Lithuania
lithuania.dish_note: Potato dumplings stuffed with meat or cold beet soup — hearty, potato-heavy cuisine influenced by German/Polish/Russian traditions.
lithuania.personality_story: Grand Duke who ruled Lithuanian Grand Duchy at its peak — largest state in Europe stretching from Baltic to Black Sea. Military genius, diplomat. National hero representing Lithuania's historical greatness before partitions.

luxembourg.name: Luxembourg
luxembourg.dish_note: Smoked pork with broad beans — hearty Luxembourgish comfort food. Or potato fritters. German/French/Belgian influenced cuisine. Moselle wines.
luxembourg.personality_story: Prime Minister (1995-2013) then President of European Commission (2014-19). Transformed Luxembourg into financial center, navigated EU politics. Controversial (tax haven facilitation) but effective. Represents Luxembourg's EU influence despite tiny size.

malawi.name: Malawi
malawi.dish_note: Thick maize porridge with vegetables/fish/meat — East/Southern African staple. Simple, starch-heavy. Lake Malawi chambo fish prized.
malawi.personality_story: First president (1964-94, 30 years). 'Life President' (1971-94) who ruled as dictator but maintained stability. Wore three-piece suits in African heat. Women wore dresses (pants banned). Ousted 1994 (referendum, elections). Died 1997. Represents authoritarian stability vs democracy.

malaysia.name: Malaysia
malaysia.dish_note: Coconut rice with anchovies, peanuts, egg, sambal — breakfast staple. Malaysian food blends Malay/Chinese/Indian excellence. Penang is food capital.
malaysia.personality_story: Prime Minister twice (1981-2003, 2018-20, 2020-22 briefly). Modernized Malaysia, built Petronas Towers, promoted 'Malaysia Boleh' (Malaysia Can). Controversial (authoritarian tendencies, Bumiputera policies) but transformative. At 92, became world's oldest leader.

mali.name: Mali
mali.dish_note: Peanut stew or rice dish — West African cuisine. Rice, millet, peanuts staple. French colonial influence.
mali.personality_story: President (2002-12) who led democratic Mali. Ousted in 2012 coup (triggered by Tuareg rebellion and army dissatisfaction). His overthrow began Mali's crisis. Died 2020. Represents Mali's democratic period before collapse.

malta.name: Malta
malta.dish_note: Rabbit stew in wine or ricotta pastries — Mediterranean cuisine with Italian/British/North African influences.
malta.personality_story: Prime Minister (1955-58, 1971-84) who negotiated independence from Britain (1964), closed British bases, and pursued non-aligned foreign policy. Controversial socialist leader who shaped modern Malta. Polarizing but transformative.

mauritania.name: Mauritania
mauritania.dish_note: Fish with rice, roasted lamb, or camel — North/West African fusion. Couscous, dates, camel milk. Arab/Black African influenced.
mauritania.personality_story: First president (1960-78) who led independence from France, unified diverse tribes, promoted Arab identity. Overthrown in coup (1978) after Western Sahara war. Died in exile (2003). Represents Mauritania's founding and early Arab-Black African tensions.

mexico.name: Mexico
mexico.dish_note: Tacos represent Mexican food globally but regional diversity is immense — mole, pozole, tamales. UNESCO heritage cuisine.
mexico.personality_story: First indigenous president (Zapotec), led Reform War, resisted French occupation (1860s), and established secular state. 'Respect for the rights of others is peace' is his famous quote. National hero representing democracy and indigenous dignity.

moldova.name: Moldova
moldova.dish_note: Polenta with stuffed cabbage rolls — hearty Romanian/Eastern European cuisine. Wine is excellent and cheap.
moldova.personality_story: Romanian poet considered national poet by both Romania and Moldova. His romantic poems are beloved. Represents shared Romanian/Moldovan cultural heritage despite political division.

monaco.name: Monaco
monaco.dish_note: Fried pastry with chard and ricotta is closest to local dish. But Monaco is Michelin-star capital — world-class French Mediterranean dining.
monaco.personality_story: Prince (1949-2005) who transformed Monaco from gambling resort to luxury tax haven. Married Grace Kelly (Hollywood actress, 1956). Expanded territory through land reclamation. His reign modernized Monaco. His son Prince Albert II rules today.

mongolia.name: Mongolia
mongolia.dish_note: Steamed mutton dumplings or meat cooked with hot stones — meat-heavy, dairy-based nomadic cuisine. Vegetables are scarce.
mongolia.personality_story: Founded Mongol Empire — largest contiguous land empire in history (13th-14th centuries). Conquered from China to Europe. Brutal warrior but also promoted trade, religious tolerance, meritocracy. National hero and source of immense pride. His face is everywhere.

montenegro.name: Montenegro
montenegro.dish_note: Smoked ham, grilled meat, or squid ink risotto — Balkan-Mediterranean fusion. Serbian/Turkish/Italian influenced.
montenegro.personality_story: Dominant politician (PM/President 1991-2023, 30+ years in power). Led independence from Serbia (2006). Accused of corruption, organized crime links but acquitted. Represents Montenegro's transition and persistent corruption. Finally out of power (2023).

morocco.name: Morocco
morocco.dish_note: Slow-cooked stew in clay pot or Friday couscous — aromatic, flavorful Berber/Arab/Mediterranean/Andalusian cuisine. Mint tea is ritual.
morocco.personality_story: King (1961-99) who ruled with iron fist during 'Years of Lead' — political repression, disappearances. Built Hassan II Mosque (world's 7th-largest). Controversial authoritarian who maintained stability. His son Mohammed VI is current king (since 1999).

mozambique.name: Mozambique
mozambique.dish_note: Grilled chicken with chili sauce or cassava leaves with shrimp — African/Portuguese/Indian fusion. Seafood is excellent on coast.
mozambique.personality_story: First president (1975-86) who led independence from Portugal. Marxist revolutionary who implemented socialist policies. Died in plane crash (1986, suspicious circumstances). National hero but his policies contributed to economic collapse. His widow Graça Machel later married Nelson Mandela.

myanmar.name: Myanmar
myanmar.dish_note: Fish broth rice noodle soup — breakfast staple. Burmese cuisine is flavorful but food insecurity is crisis post-coup.
myanmar.personality_story: Nobel Peace Prize winner (1991), democracy icon who led opposition to military rule. Released from house arrest (2010), became State Counsellor (2016-21). Failed to stop Rohingya genocide. Overthrown in 2021 coup, imprisoned. Tragic fall from grace but remains symbol of resistance.

namibia.name: Namibia
namibia.dish_note: Dried meat, BBQ, or street-grilled meat — Southern African meat-heavy cuisine with German influences (beer, pastries).
namibia.personality_story: First president (1990-2005) who led SWAPO liberation movement fighting South African occupation. Father of independence. His 15-year rule brought stability but also authoritarian tendencies. National hero representing independence struggle.

nepal.name: Nepal
nepal.dish_note: Lentil soup with rice — eaten twice daily, simple and filling. Or Tibetan dumplings (momos). Vegetarian-heavy, Indian/Tibetan influenced.
nepal.personality_story: Sherpa mountaineer who with Edmund Hillary made first confirmed ascent of Everest (1953). National hero representing Sherpa mountaineering excellence and Nepal's Himalayan identity. His son Jamling also climbed Everest.

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.dish_note: Mashed potatoes with vegetables or raw herring — simple comfort food. Cheese culture is strong. Indonesian rijsttafel reflects colonial history.
netherlands.personality_story: Jewish girl who hid from Nazis in Amsterdam (1942-44), kept diary documenting Holocaust experience. Died in Bergen-Belsen concentration camp (1945, age 15). Her diary is one of most-read books globally. Anne Frank House is pilgrimage site.

new-zealand.name: New Zealand
new-zealand.dish_note: Meringue dessert, meat pies, or Māori earth oven feast — modern cuisine is farm-to-table, seafood-focused. Wine is world-class.
new-zealand.personality_story: First person (with Tenzing Norgay) to reach summit of Mount Everest (1953). National hero representing Kiwi can-do attitude and mountaineering excellence. His face was on NZD $5 note. Philanthropist who built schools in Nepal.
sectors: Film production (Lord of the Rings, Avatar)

nicaragua.name: Nicaragua
nicaragua.dish_note: Rice and beans or large tamale — simple, corn-based Central American cuisine. Similar to neighbors.
nicaragua.personality_story: Revolutionary leader who fought US occupation (1920s-30s). Assassinated 1934. Sandinista movement (FSLN) named after him. National hero representing anti-imperialism. Daniel Ortega's FSLN betrayed Sandino's legacy by becoming dictatorship.

niger.name: Niger
niger.dish_note: Millet couscous with groundnut and moringa sauce. Tuareg nomadic culture: millet with camel milk. Hausa spiced stews dominate urban cooking.
niger.personality_story: Niger's first president (1960–1974), he led independence from France and initially governed with restraint. He became a respected Pan-African voice — mediating conflicts across the continent, proposing a francophone economic community, and brokering the 1973 Vietnam peace agreement. Then the 1973 Sahel famine killed 100,000 Nigeriens while his government concealed the scale. A military coup in 1974 overthrew him. He spent 11 years under house arrest. His story encapsulates Niger's arc: promising independence, elite failure, and the coup cycle that has never stopped.

nigeria.name: Nigeria
nigeria.dish_note: Tomato rice (vs Ghana rivalry), melon seed soup, or spicy grilled meat — diverse, spicy, flavorful cuisine.
nigeria.rate: 1 USD ≈ 1,500 NGN (official, black market much higher)
nigeria.personality_story: Musician and activist who created Afrobeat genre, criticized military dictatorships, and lived in commune (Kalakuta Republic). Arrested 200+ times. Died 1997. His music and rebellion shaped Nigerian identity. Sons Femi and Seun continue legacy.

north-macedonia.name: North Macedonia
north-macedonia.dish_note: Baked beans or red pepper relish — Balkan cuisine, grilled meats, burek, Turkish/Greek influenced.
north-macedonia.personality_story: Born in Skopje (1910) as Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu. Became Catholic nun, worked with poor in Calcutta, won Nobel Peace Prize (1979). National icon despite spending life abroad. Memorial House in Skopje honors her.

norway.name: Norway
norway.dish_note: Mutton stew, brown cheese, or fermented fish — traditional but modern cuisine is New Nordic (seasonal, local, seafood). Salmon is iconic.
norway.personality_story: Polar explorer who led first expedition to reach South Pole (1911, beating Scott). Also first to traverse Northwest Passage. National hero representing Norwegian exploration and resilience. Disappeared 1928 during Arctic rescue mission.

oman.name: Oman
oman.dish_note: Underground-roasted lamb or spiced rice with meat — Arabic cuisine with Indian/Persian/East African influences. Seafood is excellent.
oman.personality_story: Sultan (1970-2020) who modernized Oman from medieval backwater to modern state. Overthrew his father (1970) and ended isolation. Built roads, schools, hospitals. Maintained neutrality in regional conflicts. Beloved leader whose 50-year rule transformed nation. Died 2020; cousin Haitham succeeded.

pakistan.name: Pakistan
pakistan.dish_note: Spiced rice with meat or slow-cooked stew — flavorful, meat-heavy Mughal/Afghan influenced cuisine. Street food is vibrant.
pakistan.personality_story: Founder of Pakistan ('Quaid-e-Azam' — Great Leader) who led Muslim League demanding separate Muslim state during partition (1947). First Governor-General. Died 1948. National hero. His mausoleum in Karachi is pilgrimage site.

palestine.name: Palestine
palestine.dish_note: Roasted chicken-sumac, upside-down rice, or cheese pastry — Levantine cuisine. Olive oil, za'atar. Palestinian culinary identity.
palestine.currency: Israeli new shekel (ILS), Jordanian dinar (JOD), US dollar (USD)
palestine.personality_story: PLO leader (1969-2004), Palestinian nationalism icon. Nobel Peace Prize (1994, with Rabin, Peres) for Oslo Accords. Founded Fatah. President of Palestinian Authority (1994-2004). Controversial — freedom fighter or terrorist depending on view. Died 2004 (poisoning suspected but unproven). Represents Palestinian struggle.

panama.name: Panama
panama.dish_note: Chicken soup with yuca or ceviche — Latin American/Caribbean cuisine. Seafood is excellent. International food widely available.
panama.personality_story: Military leader (1968-81) who negotiated Torrijos-Carter Treaties (1977) transferring Canal from US to Panama (completed 1999). Populist dictator who improved rural infrastructure. Died in plane crash (1981). National hero for Canal sovereignty.

paraguay.name: Paraguay
paraguay.dish_note: Cornbread (despite 'soup' name) or cheese bread — simple, corn-based Guaraní-influenced cuisine. Tereré (cold mate) is national drink.
paraguay.personality_story: Military dictator (1954-89) — longest-ruling dictator in South American history (35 years). Brutal regime with torture, disappearances, but also infrastructure development. Overthrown 1989. His legacy is dictatorship that shaped modern Paraguay. Died in Brazilian exile 2006.

peru.name: Peru
peru.dish_note: Raw fish in lime or stir-fried beef — world-class fusion cuisine (indigenous/Spanish/Chinese/Japanese). Lima is culinary capital.
peru.personality_story: Inca emperor (1438-71) who expanded empire and built Machu Picchu. Transformed small kingdom into South America's largest empire. His architectural and administrative achievements shaped Inca civilization. National symbol of indigenous greatness.

philippines.name: Philippines
philippines.dish_note: Vinegar-braised meat, sour soup, or roasted pig — Malay/Chinese/Spanish fusion. Sweet-salty-sour flavors. Street food vibrant.
philippines.personality_story: National hero, polymath, novelist whose writings (Noli Me Tángere) inspired revolution against Spanish rule. Executed by Spain (1896, age 35). His martyrdom galvanized independence movement. Represents Filipino nationalism and intellectual resistance.

poland.name: Poland
poland.dish_note: Dumplings, hunter's stew, or sour rye soup — hearty, meat-heavy, cabbage/potato-based cuisine. Vodka is institution.
poland.personality_story: Solidarity trade union leader who led strikes at Gdańsk shipyard (1980), won Nobel Peace Prize (1983), and became first post-communist president (1990-95). His leadership helped topple communism. National hero though later controversies emerged.

portugal.name: Portugal
portugal.dish_note: Salted cod (1,000+ preparations) or custard tarts — seafood-focused cuisine. Wine (port, vinho verde) is excellent.
portugal.personality_story: Poet and writer who wrote under 75+ heteronyms (alter egos with distinct styles). Represented Portuguese saudade and intellectual complexity. Modernist icon. Statue in Lisbon's Chiado honors him. His poetry captures Portuguese soul.

qatar.name: Qatar
qatar.dish_note: Spiced rice with meat or wheat-meat porridge — Arabic Gulf cuisine. International food dominates due to expats.
qatar.personality: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
qatar.personality_story: Emir (1995-2013) who transformed Qatar from small emirate to global player. Founded Al Jazeera, invested gas wealth strategically, bid for World Cup. Abdicated voluntarily to son Tamim (2013). His vision shaped modern Qatar.

republic-of-the-congo.name: Republic of the Congo
republic-of-the-congo.dish_note: Chicken in palm nut sauce or cassava leaves — Central African staple. Cassava, plantains, palm oil, fish. French colonial influence.
republic-of-the-congo.personality_story: President (1979-92, 1997-present, 40+ years total). Won 1997 civil war (with Angolan support), returned to power. Changed constitution to remove age/term limits. Rules authoritatively. M'Bochi ethnicity (north). Accumulated massive wealth. Represents Congo's oil-fueled autocracy.

romania.name: Romania
romania.dish_note: Cabbage rolls or grilled meat rolls — hearty pork/polenta-based cuisine. Balkan/Turkish/Hungarian influenced. Wine is cheap.
romania.personality_story: Communist dictator (1965-89) whose megalomania bankrupted country (built massive Palace of Parliament, demolished historic Bucharest). Brutal Securitate secret police. 1989 revolution overthrew and executed him. His legacy is trauma and Palace (world's 2nd-largest building).

russia.name: Russia
russia.dish_note: Beet soup, dumplings, or pancakes — hearty potato/cabbage/beet-based cuisine. Soviet nostalgia foods persist.
russia.personality_story: Novelist whose 'War and Peace' and 'Anna Karenina' are masterpieces of world literature. Aristocrat who questioned society, embraced Christian anarchism. His works explored Russian soul, morality, history. Represents Russia's literary golden age.

rwanda.name: Rwanda
rwanda.dish_note: Maize porridge or cassava leaves — simple, filling cuisine. Beans, plantains, sweet potatoes staple. Meat is luxury.
rwanda.personality_story: President since 2000 (military leader since 1994 stopping genocide). Led RPF that ended genocide. Transformed Rwanda from ruins to development success. But authoritarian — opposition crushed, term limits removed. Complex legacy: developer and dictator.

san-marino.name: San Marino
san-marino.dish: Torta Tre Monti / Pasta e Ceci
san-marino.dish_note: Three-tower layered cake or pasta-chickpeas — Italian cuisine. Emilia-Romagna/Marche influenced. Piadina, local wines.
san-marino.personality_story: Legendary founder (traditionally 301 AD). Christian stonemason who fled persecution, founded community on Mount Titano. San Marino claims to be world's oldest republic based on this legend. Whether historically accurate or myth, Marinus is national symbol of independence and Christian refuge.

saudi-arabia.name: Saudi Arabia
saudi-arabia.dish_note: Spiced rice with meat or Yemeni-style rice — Arabic Gulf cuisine. Rice, meat, dates staple. International food available.
saudi-arabia.personality_story: Crown Prince (since 2017) and de facto ruler. Architect of Vision 2030 modernization — women driving, cinemas, tourism. But also Khashoggi murder (2018, journalist killed in consulate), Yemen war, and authoritarian crackdowns. Divisive figure: reformer or dictator?

senegal.name: Senegal
senegal.dish_note: Fish-rice-vegetable dish or onion-marinated chicken — West African rice/fish/peanut-based cuisine. French colonial influence.
senegal.personality_story: First president (1960-80), poet, and intellectual who championed Négritude movement (African cultural pride). Voluntarily stepped down after 20 years — rare in Africa. Represents Senegal's intellectual tradition and peaceful democracy. French Academy member.

serbia.name: Serbia
serbia.dish_note: Grilled meat sausages or Serbian burger — Balkan grilled meat cuisine. Kajmak, ajvar, Turkish/Austro-Hungarian influenced. Rakija culture.
serbia.personality_story: Serbian-American inventor and electrical engineer whose AC current, Tesla coil, and numerous inventions shaped modern world. Born in Serbia (then Austria-Hungary), worked in US. National hero representing Serbian genius. Airport named after him.

sierra-leone.name: Sierra Leone
sierra-leone.dish: Cassava Leaves / Jollof Rice / Groundnut Stew
sierra-leone.dish_note: Cassava greens or rice dishes — West African staple. Rice, cassava, palm oil, groundnuts. Krio (freed slave) influenced.
sierra-leone.personality_story: President (1996-97, 1998-2007) who led Sierra Leone through war's end. Ousted in 1997 coup, returned 1998. Signed Lomé Peace Accord (1999) granting amnesty to rebels (controversial). Presided over Special Court trials. Nobel Peace Prize nomination. Died 2014. Represents peace process.

singapore.name: Singapore
singapore.dish: Hainanese Chicken Rice / Chili Crab / Laksa
singapore.dish_note: Chicken rice, chili crab, or spicy noodle soup — multicultural hawker food paradise. Michelin-starred street food exists.
singapore.personality_story: Founding father and first Prime Minister (1959-90) who transformed Singapore from third-world to first-world in one generation. Authoritarian but effective — crushed opposition, controlled media, built meritocracy. Died 2015. His model: development before democracy.

slovakia.name: Slovakia
slovakia.dish_note: Potato dumplings with sheep cheese and bacon — hearty Central European comfort food. Hungarian/Austrian influenced.
slovakia.personality_story: Communist leader who led Prague Spring (1968) — liberalization attempt crushed by Soviet invasion. His 'socialism with human face' inspired but failed. Symbol of Slovak resistance to Soviet control. Post-1989, he supported Velvet Revolution.

slovenia.name: Slovenia
slovenia.dish_note: Rolled walnut pastry or Carniolan sausage — Central European cuisine with Italian influence. Strong wine culture.
slovenia.personality_story: National poet whose works defined Slovenian language and identity. 'Zdravljica' (A Toast) became national anthem. He represents Slovenian cultural renaissance and linguistic independence. Prešeren Day (Feb 8) is national cultural holiday.

somalia.name: Somalia
somalia.dish_note: Fragrant spiced rice with goat or camel, sourdough flatbread, and fresh camel milk. Indian Ocean trade (Arab, Indian, Persian) defines the cuisine.
somalia.rate: 1 USD ≈ 571 SOS (official) — USD dominates in practice
somalia.personality_story: Elected president in 2012 and re-elected in 2022, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud represents something unusual in Somali politics: a civilian intellectual, not a warlord or military figure. A university rector and civil society leader, he has worked to extend federal authority and launched the first coordinated military offensive against al-Shabaab in a decade. Progress is real but fragile — he governs from behind blast walls, his authority dependent on African Union troops and clan coalition-building. The fact that Somalia now has a functioning electoral process, however imperfect, is itself remarkable given where the country was in 2000.

south-africa.name: South Africa
south-africa.dish_note: Spiced meat, BBQ, or curry in bread — fusion cuisine (indigenous/Dutch/Malay/Indian). Wine is world-class.
south-africa.personality_story: Anti-apartheid icon imprisoned 27 years (Robben Island), became first Black president (1994-99), led reconciliation through Truth and Reconciliation Commission. Nobel Peace Prize 1993. 'Madiba' is beloved globally. Died 2013. His legacy is reconciliation despite injustice.

south-korea.name: South Korea
south-korea.dish_note: Fermented cabbage accompanies every meal, or mixed rice bowl, or grilled meats — complex, spicy, communal cuisine. Fried chicken + beer is pastime.
south-korea.personality_story: President/dictator (1961-79) who led economic development from poverty to industrialization. Authoritarian rule but created 'Miracle on the Han River.' Assassinated 1979. Controversial legacy — economic success vs human rights abuses. His daughter Park Geun-hye later became president.

spain.name: Spain
spain.dish_note: Valencian rice dish, cured ham, or small plates — regional diversity immense. Mediterranean diet, UNESCO heritage. Wine/olive oil world-class.
spain.personality_story: Artist who co-founded Cubism and created 'Guernica' (anti-war masterpiece depicting Spanish Civil War bombing). One of most influential artists of 20th century. Represents Spanish creative genius. Born Málaga, worked in Barcelona and Paris.

sri-lanka.name: Sri Lanka
sri-lanka.dish_note: Rice with multiple curries — extremely spicy, coconut-based cuisine. Indian/Portuguese/Dutch influenced. Hoppers for breakfast.
sri-lanka.personality_story: British science fiction author ('2001: A Space Odyssey') who moved to Sri Lanka (1956) and lived there until death (2008). Popularized Sri Lanka globally. His residence in Colombo became cultural landmark. Represents Sri Lanka's attraction for creative types.

sudan.name: Sudan
sudan.dish_note: Fava beans with lemon and oil — the national breakfast at every income level. Sorghum flatbread (Kisra) with meat or groundnut sauce. Sudanese spiced tea culture is central to social life.
sudan.personality_story: Ruled Sudan for 30 years (1989–2019) after an Islamist coup. Indicted by the International Criminal Court for genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes in Darfur — the first sitting head of state to be indicted by the ICC. He killed an estimated 300,000 people in Darfur (2003–2005) using the Janjaweed militias — the predecessors of today's RSF, commanded by his own ally Hemedti. He was overthrown in 2019 by the same generals he had empowered. He died in prison in January 2025 awaiting an ICC extradition that never came.
sectors: Gold mining (3rd-largest in Africa pre-war — largely informal now)
Gum arabic (75–80% of global supply — continues via smuggling)

suriname.name: Suriname
suriname.dish_note: Root vegetable casserole, Indian flatbread, or Javanese fried rice — world's most diverse cuisine. Hindustani/Javanese/Creole/Chinese/indigenous fusion.
suriname.personality_story: Military strongman/president (1980-87 military rule, 2010-20 elected). 1982 'December Murders' — executed 15 opponents. Convicted in absentia for drug trafficking (Netherlands). 2019: convicted of December Murders (20 years) but remained president. Fled after 2020 election loss. Represents Suriname's authoritarian, corrupt past.

sweden.name: Sweden
sweden.dish_note: Meatballs, cured salmon, or fermented herring — simple, fish-heavy cuisine. Fika culture (coffee break) is institution. New Nordic movement.
sweden.personality_story: Inventor of dynamite who became wealthy from explosives. His will established Nobel Prizes (Peace, Literature, Physics, Chemistry, Medicine/Physiology, later Economics). Prizes awarded in Stockholm (except Peace in Oslo). Represents Swedish innovation and humanitarian values.

switzerland.name: Switzerland
switzerland.dish_note: Melted cheese, potato pancake — hearty cheese/potato-based cuisine. Chocolate is world-class. Dining out is prohibitively expensive.
switzerland.personality_story: Tennis legend with 20 Grand Slam titles. Embodiment of Swiss precision, grace, excellence. Global ambassador for Switzerland. Retired 2022. Represents Swiss pursuit of perfection and international success.

syria.name: Syria
syria.dish_note: Bulgur-meat, grilled meat, or salad — Levantine cuisine. But food insecurity is crisis. Sieges caused starvation.
syria.rate: 1 USD ≈ 13,500 SYP (official), black market much higher
syria.personality_story: President since 2000 (inherited from father Hafez). Initially seemed reformist (ophthalmologist, Western-educated). Crushed 2011 protests brutally, triggering civil war. Used chemical weapons, barrel bombs, torture, siege starvation against own people. War criminal per international observers. Backed by Russia, Iran. Won war but rules ruins.

taiwan.name: Taiwan
taiwan.dish: Beef Noodle Soup / Bubble Tea / Xiao Long Bao
taiwan.dish_note: Beef noodles, bubble tea (invented here), or soup dumplings — fusion of Chinese regional cuisines, Japanese influence. Night market culture.
taiwan.personality_story: President (2016-24), first female president of Taiwan. Led during heightened China tensions. Strengthened US ties, modernized military. DPP (pro-independence party). Navigated Taiwan through geopolitical threats. Represents Taiwan's democratic identity vs China's authoritarianism.

tajikistan.name: Tajikistan
tajikistan.dish_note: Rice pilaf, bread-yogurt, or meat pastries — Central Asian-Persian fusion. Rice, bread, lamb. Persian/Uzbek/Russian influenced.
tajikistan.personality_story: President since 1994 (30 years). Rose during civil war (1992-97), consolidated power as authoritarian. Eliminated opposition (jailed Islamic Renaissance Party 2015), controls media, changed constitution for dynastic succession. Son Rustam is Dushanbe mayor (heir apparent). Represents Tajikistan's authoritarianism and poverty under strongman rule.

tanzania.name: Tanzania
tanzania.dish: Ugali with stew / Nyama Choma / Pilau
tanzania.dish_note: Maize porridge, grilled meat, or spiced rice — East African staple. Arab/Indian/Portuguese influenced (Zanzibar spice trade).
tanzania.personality_story: First president (1964-85), 'Mwalimu' (teacher). Led independence from Britain, unified Tanganyika + Zanzibar. Promoted African socialism (Ujamaa — familyhood, collectivization). Loved for integrity, peaceful transition (resigned voluntarily 1985). Legacy mixed: unity vs economic failure. Translated Shakespeare to Swahili.

thailand.name: Thailand
thailand.dish: Pad Thai / Tom Yum / Som Tam
thailand.dish_note: Stir-fried noodles, spicy soup, or papaya salad — world-class street food. Balance of sweet/sour/salty/spicy. Regional diversity.
thailand.personality_story: King (1946-2016) — world's longest-reigning monarch. Beloved figure who represented stability through coups and crises. His son King Rama X (current) is controversial — lives in Germany, extravagant lifestyle. Lèse-majesté laws forbid criticism.

timor-leste.name: Timor-Leste
timor-leste.dish_note: Grilled fish, corn-beans, or curry — simple cuisine. Fish, corn, cassava. Portuguese/Indonesian influenced. Malnutrition widespread.
timor-leste.personality_story: Independence hero, resistance leader (Fretilin, CNRT), imprisoned by Indonesia (1992-99). First president (2002-07), prime minister (2007-15, 2023-present). Nobel Peace Prize nominee. Represents Timor-Leste's struggle and independence. National icon despite governance challenges.

togo.name: Togo
togo.dish: Fufu with Sauce d'Arachide / Gboma Dessi
togo.dish_note: Pounded cassava/yam with peanut sauce or spinach stew — West African staple. Fufu, stews, grilled fish. French colonial influence.
togo.personality_story: Military dictator/president (1967-2005, 38 years). Longest-ruling African leader at death. Military coup (1967), authoritarian rule, accumulated wealth, survived assassination attempts. Died 2005 (plane crash returning from abroad). Son Faure succeeded (military installed him). Dynasty continues.

trinidad-and-tobago.name: Trinidad and Tobago
trinidad-and-tobago.dish_note: Fried bread with chickpeas, curry flatbread, or shark sandwich — fusion cuisine. Indian/African/Chinese/Creole influenced.
trinidad-and-tobago.personality_story: Nobel Prize Literature winner (2001). Born in Trinidad to Indian indentured labor descendants. Novels explored colonialism, post-colonial identity, displacement. 'A House for Mr Biswas' is masterpiece. Controversial figure (acerbic, critical of Trinidad). Represents Indo-Trinidadian intellectual tradition.

tunisia.name: Tunisia
tunisia.dish_note: Semolina with vegetables/meat or fried pastry — North African cuisine. Berber/Arab/Turkish/French/Italian influenced. Harissa chili paste ubiquitous.
tunisia.personality_story: First president (1957-87) who modernized Tunisia — women's rights, education, secular state. Authoritarian but progressive. Ousted in 1987. Represents post-independence modernization. His legacy is secular, educated Tunisia (now threatened).

turkey.name: Turkey
turkey.dish_note: Grilled meat, small plates, or savory pastries — Ottoman legacy cuisine. Balkan/Middle Eastern/Central Asian/Mediterranean fusion. Çay culture.
turkey.personality_story: Founder of modern Turkey (1923), abolished Ottoman Caliphate, secularized state, modernized society (alphabet, women's rights, education). Father of Turks (Atatürk). His secular legacy is being eroded by Erdogan's Islamism. Criticizing Atatürk is criminal offense.

turkmenistan.name: Turkmenistan
turkmenistan.dish_note: Rice pilaf, grilled meat, or dumplings — Central Asian nomadic cuisine. Rice, lamb, bread. Persian/Russian influenced.
turkmenistan.rate: 1 USD ≈ 3.5 TMT (official), black market much higher
turkmenistan.personality_story: President (1991-2006, 'President for Life'). Created extreme personality cult: renamed himself Turkmenbashi ('Leader of all Turkmen'), renamed months, built golden statues, wrote Ruhnama (mandatory study), banned beards/opera/ballet. Died 2006 (heart failure). Legacy is totalitarianism and absurdity. Berdimuhamedow continued/intensified cult.

uganda.name: Uganda
uganda.dish_note: Steamed plantains, maize porridge, or egg-chapati roll — East African staple food. Simple, filling cuisine.
uganda.personality_story: Brutal dictator (1971-79) whose regime killed 300,000 Ugandans. Expelled Asians (1972, 60,000 fled), ruined economy, created terror state. 'Butcher of Uganda.' Overthrown 1979, fled to Saudi Arabia. His legacy is trauma and cautionary tale of tyranny.

ukraine.name: Ukraine
ukraine.dish_note: Beet soup or dumplings — hearty Ukrainian cuisine. UNESCO recognized borscht (2022) as Ukrainian heritage (vs Russian claims).
ukraine.personality_story: President since 2019 (former comedian, 'Servant of the People' actor). Became wartime leader Feb 2022 — refused US evacuation offer ('I need ammunition, not a ride'), rallied resistance, secured Western weapons. His leadership inspired global support. Represents Ukrainian courage.

united-arab-emirates.name: United Arab Emirates
united-arab-emirates.dish_note: Wheat-meat porridge or spiced rice — Arabian Gulf cuisine. International food dominates due to expats. Dining is expensive.
united-arab-emirates.personality: Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan
united-arab-emirates.personality_story: Founding father of UAE (1971), ruler of Abu Dhabi (1966-2004). Unified seven emirates, invested oil wealth wisely, modernized country. Beloved 'Father of the Nation.' His vision transformed desert to first-world nation. Died 2004.

united-kingdom.name: United Kingdom
united-kingdom.dish: Fish and Chips / Chicken Tikka Masala / Sunday Roast
united-kingdom.dish_note: Fried fish or curry (invented in UK) or roast dinner — British cuisine improved from bland reputation. Indian/Chinese/Turkish integral.
united-kingdom.personality_story: Prime Minister during WWII (1940-45, 1951-55) whose leadership ('We shall never surrender' speech) rallied Britain during darkest hour. Nobel Prize Literature. Icon of British resolve. Controversial for colonialism views. 'Greatest Briton' polls.

united-states.name: United States
united-states.dish_note: Burger, regional BBQ, or pie — immigrant fusion cuisine. Italian/Mexican/Chinese/soul food integral. Fast food is export. Portions huge.
united-states.personality_story: Civil rights leader whose nonviolent resistance fought racial segregation. 'I Have a Dream' speech (1963). Assassinated 1968. Nobel Peace Prize 1964. His legacy is racial justice movement. MLK Day is federal holiday. Represents American ideals vs reality struggle.

uruguay.name: Uruguay
uruguay.dish_note: BBQ beef or steak sandwich — meat-heavy cuisine. Highest beef consumption per capita globally (50kg/year). Mate tea culture. Italian influence.
uruguay.personality_story: President (2010-15), former guerrilla (imprisoned 14 years under dictatorship), lived in farmhouse on $12k/year salary (donated rest). 'World's poorest president' or 'humble president.' Legalized marijuana. Icon of humility, progressive values. Represents Uruguay's unique political culture.

uzbekistan.name: Uzbekistan
uzbekistan.dish_note: Rice pilaf with meat, noodle soup, or meat pastries — Central Asian cuisine. Persian/Russian/Turkish influenced. Bread (non) sacred.
uzbekistan.personality_story: Turco-Mongol conqueror who built empire from Samarkand (capital). Built stunning mosques, madrassas (Registan Square, Gur-e-Amir mausoleum). Brutal conqueror but patron of arts, architecture. National hero representing Uzbek greatness. His legacy is Samarkand's magnificence.
sectors: Agriculture (cotton, though forced labor being addressed)

vatican.name: Vatican City
vatican.dish_note: Too small for cuisine. Residents eat Italian food. Vatican cafeterias serve Roman meals. Pope Francis eats communally, simply.
vatican.personality_story: Pope since 2013 (first Jesuit pope, first from Americas — Argentina, first Francis name). Born Jorge Mario Bergoglio. Progressive reputation (emphasis on poor, environment, mercy) but maintains doctrine. Scandal management (abuse cover-ups). Represents Catholic Church's current face.

venezuela.name: Venezuela
venezuela.dish_note: Corn cakes or beef-beans-rice — Venezuelan cuisine. But food scarcity is crisis ('Maduro diet' — people lost 11kg average 2017).
venezuela.rate: 1 USD ≈ 36 VES (official, black market much higher)
venezuela.personality_story: President (1999-2013) who led Bolivarian Revolution — socialist policies, oil wealth redistribution, anti-US rhetoric. Initially reduced poverty but sowed economic collapse seeds. Died 2013 (cancer). Maduro (VP) continued policies with catastrophic results. Chávez is divisive — hero or destroyer.

vietnam.name: Vietnam
vietnam.dish_note: Noodle soup, baguette sandwich, or grilled pork — world-class cuisine. Balance of flavors, fresh herbs, French colonial influence.
vietnam.personality_story: Revolutionary leader who led independence from France (1954) and reunification war vs US-backed South (1975, died 1969 before victory). 'Uncle Ho' is revered — mausoleum in Hanoi, cities/streets named after him. Founded communist state. National hero representing independence and anti-imperialism.

yemen.name: Yemen
yemen.dish_note: Meat stew or honey cake — Yemeni cuisine. But 17M+ face food insecurity. Famine conditions exist. Cuisine is memory.
yemen.rate: 1 USD ≈ 1,050 YER (varies by region, multiple exchange rates)
yemen.personality_story: President (1978-2012, 33 years) ousted in Arab Spring (2011). Initially allied with Houthis against successor Hadi, then switched sides (2017) and was killed by Houthis. His legacy is corruption, patronage networks, and setting stage for civil war.

zambia.name: Zambia
zambia.dish_note: Thick maize porridge with vegetables/meat — Southern African staple. Simple, filling cuisine. Eaten with hands.
zambia.personality_story: First president (1964-91) who led independence from Britain. Initially socialist (nationalized copper), later liberalized. Peacefully left power (1991 election loss) — rare in Africa. Died 2021. National hero representing independence and democratic tradition.

zimbabwe.name: Zimbabwe
zimbabwe.dish_note: Thick maize porridge with vegetables/meat/kapenta — Southern African staple. Simple cuisine. British colonial influence.
zimbabwe.rate: 1 USD ≈ 13,500 ZWL (official, black market much higher)
zimbabwe.personality_story: Liberation hero who became dictator (1980-2017, 37 years). Initially praised, later destroyed economy (land seizures 2000, hyperinflation), crushed opposition (Gukurahundi massacres 1980s killed 20,000 Ndebele), rigged elections. Ousted 2017 coup (army, replaced by VP Mnangagwa). Died 2019. Legacy is economic ruin and authoritarianism.
